episodes.title: Hydra of Lerna
episodes.hotspot: Field heat and energy contribute 44.5% of the baseline footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: A 3.2 t, nine-headed Hydra reconstructed as a hazardous field-control event: cutting is only the first step, while cauterisation, logistics and containment create a 1.35 t CO₂e footprint.
episodes.functionalUnit: One Hydra neutralisation and containment event, modelled as one field response cycle from arrival to the immortal head sealed under the boulder and the containment pit closed.

evidence.basis: The canonical nine-headed Hydra and its regeneration problem define the intervention logic. The approved episode uses an 11 m, 3.2 t semi-aquatic reconstruction and models neutralisation as cutting, thermal cauterisation and controlled containment with modern field-response flows and emission-factor proxies.
evidence.uncertainty: Body mass scales fuel, lime, sheeting and freight and moves the result from 1.01 to 1.88 t CO₂e; the quicklime emission factor is a secondary proxy sensitivity that does not change the hotspot story.

episodes.title: The Garden of the Hesperides
episodes.hotspot: The 10 µm gold gilding layer contributes 296.4 kg CO₂e, or 88.2% of the modeled total.
episodes.featuredDescription: Three golden apples reconstructed as one annual guarded orchard service: a 10 µm gold skin is enough to make primary gold dominate the 336 kg CO₂e baseline while water, electricity and freight remain minor.
episodes.functionalUnit: One annual guarded presentation of three golden apples from the Hesperidean orchard gate.

evidence.basis: The documented myth constrains the guarded golden fruit and Ladon. The approved episode reconstructs three 80 mm apples, a 10 µm gold surface and one year of western Mediterranean orchard support using literature benchmarks, engineering assumptions, DEFRA 2026 factors and a separately disclosed primary-gold proxy.
evidence.uncertainty: Gold thickness and gold-source intensity dominate interpretation: the physical sensitivity spans 188–781 kg CO₂e and the gold-factor sensitivity spans 139–484 kg CO₂e.

episodes.title: Santa's Sleigh
episodes.hotspot: Reindeer forage contributes 177.7 kg CO₂e, or 67% of the baseline footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: A reusable 4.2 m sleigh reconstructed as a one-night delivery system: 267 kg CO₂e per Christmas Eve mission, with reindeer forage dominating the baseline and feeding-rate and harness assumptions controlling the main sensitivities.
episodes.functionalUnit: One reusable airborne gift-delivery sleigh completing one Christmas Eve mission.

evidence.basis: The approved episode uses a canonical eight-reindeer motive team and reconstructs one 4.2 m reusable sleigh with a 160 kg laminated-wood body, 40 kg steel runners and brackets, a 30 kg leather/textile harness and a twelve-mission lifetime. DEFRA 2026 is prioritized for physical material, forage and logistics flows, with declared modern proxies where no dedicated factor exists.
evidence.uncertainty: Feeding rate moves the total from 208 to 326 kg CO₂e, while changing the harness factor moves it from 211 to 351 kg CO₂e. Magic flight energy remains excluded rather than receiving an invented emission factor.

episodes.title: Baba Yaga's Hut
episodes.hotspot: Metal hardware and leg bracing contribute 1.72 t CO₂e, or 46.1% of the baseline footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: A 5.87 t Slavic walking forest hut reconstructed from logs, metal bracing, chimney, glazing and commissioning flows: the 3.73 t CO₂e baseline is driven by the structure that lets the cabin stand on legs, not by magic.
episodes.functionalUnit: One reconstructed walking hut, delivered and commissioned once (reference flow: one cabin; 30-year service context).

evidence.basis: Slavic folklore supplies the walking-hut form while the approved episode supplies an explicit engineering reconstruction: a 3.6 × 3.0 m log-cabin envelope, 5.87 t modeled mass, two structural bird-leg supports, workshop electricity, freight and installation. DEFRA 2026 is prioritized for the disclosed physical flows and modern proxies are declared where exact factors do not exist.
evidence.uncertainty: Physical scaling is the largest uncertainty: the mass sensitivity moves the result from 2.77 to 5.55 t CO₂e. Material origin is also consequential, shifting the modeled footprint from 1.62 t CO₂e with reused timber and recycled metal to 4.20 t CO₂e in the high-material-intensity case.

episodes.title: Hermes Sandals
episodes.hotspot: Gold leaf contributes 80.2% of the baseline with only 0.3% of product mass.
episodes.featuredDescription: One 0.682 kg pair of winged talaria reconstructed as engineered footwear: 63.5 kg CO₂e cradle-to-delivered-gate, with two grams of gold leaf driving 80.2% of the footprint.
episodes.functionalUnit: One pair of winged talaria enabling one courier mission.

evidence.basis: The Greek myth constrains the winged courier footwear. The approved episode reconstructs one 0.682 kg pair with leather, bronze/brass wing frames, feather/textile vanes, a 2.0 g gold-leaf finish, workshop utilities, packaging and road/sea freight, prioritising DEFRA 2026 and declaring an external primary-gold proxy.
evidence.uncertainty: Gold intensity and gilding mass control the baseline: changing gold from 0.5 g to 5.0 g moves the total from 25.3 to 139.9 kg CO₂e. Leather-factor choice is the second material uncertainty, moving the modeled total from 59.3 to 136.0 kg CO₂e.

episodes.title: Pandora's Jar
episodes.hotspot: Kiln energy and freight together account for 49.9% of the baseline footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: One 45 L sealed pithos reconstructed as clay, metal, seal, workshop energy, packing and freight: 26.0 kg CO₂e from creation to first opening, with kiln energy and transport jointly driving 49.9% of the baseline.
episodes.functionalUnit: One sealed 45 L ceramic pithos delivered to a household and opened once, covering creation to first opening, with the non-physical payload explicitly cut off.

evidence.basis: The approved episode constrains the subject as a 0.55 m high, 0.42 m diameter, 45 L sealed terracotta pithos with 22.0 kg fired clay, 1.2 kg metal lid and fittings, a wax/resin seal, workshop energy, packing and road freight. Physical emission factors are disclosed as DEFRA 2026 proxies, while kiln intensity uses the CORDIS DREAM ceramic-sector benchmark.
evidence.uncertainty: Kiln intensity is the principal model risk: the reported efficient and high craft-kiln cases move the total from 23.6 to 40.1 kg CO₂e. Freight distance is also material, with the reported long-delivery case reaching 32.4 kg CO₂e.

episodes.title: Bifrost
episodes.hotspot: Electricity contributes 95.2% of the baseline footprint; the red fire-guard is the largest single modeled flow at 73.7 kg CO₂e.
episodes.featuredDescription: One 10-minute Bifrost crossing window reconstructed as a reusable two-gate light bridge: 120.3 kg CO₂e per activation, with electricity at 95.2% and the red fire-guard the largest modeled flow.
episodes.functionalUnit: One controlled Bifrost activation enabling a 10-minute crossing window for one expedition transfer.

evidence.basis: The approved episode models Bifrost as a reusable two-gate light-bridge apparatus with a 1,200 m visible corridor, 3.0 m walkable band, basalt plinths, bronze rings, emerald prism lenses, three translucent corridor bands and a red-orange thermal exclusion strand. DEFRA 2026 is the priority factor set; dimensions, mass, power and duration are engineering assumptions, and the red fire-guard is declared as a narrative proxy.
evidence.uncertainty: The red fire-guard is the main physical uncertainty: the cooler and hotter strand cases move the result to 83.4 and 194.0 kg CO₂e. Electricity carbon intensity is the main data lever, with the reported grid cases spanning 28.7 to 177.5 kg CO₂e.

episodes.title: The Argo
episodes.hotspot: Sail + rigging contributes 50.2% of the baseline footprint; wood procurement contributes 41.7%.
episodes.featuredDescription: One 28.5 m Argo-class fifty-oared vessel and one Pagasae–Colchis–Pagasae expedition: 10.66 t CO₂e per build-and-voyage functional unit, with a conservative sail-and-rigging proxy dominating while direct propulsion uses no purchased fuel.
episodes.functionalUnit: Build and equip one Argo-class fifty-oared vessel and complete one Pagasae-Colchis-Pagasae expedition under oar and sail.

evidence.basis: Argonautes 2008 provides the principal technical reconstruction for the 28.5 m vessel, 50 oars, 8 m mast and 55 m² sail. The approved episode freezes a 16.50 t wood reconstruction plus declared sail/rigging, minor-metal, stone-anchor and inbound-freight assumptions, then applies UK Government GHG Conversion Factors 2026 exact rows to the modeled physical flows.
evidence.uncertainty: The DEFRA Clothing factor used for woven sailcloth and natural-fibre rigging is explicitly the highest-uncertainty factor and drives 50.2% of baseline GWP. The reported wood-mass sensitivity spans 9.94–11.37 t CO₂e and the HGV-factor sensitivity spans 10.55–11.13 t CO₂e without overturning the hotspot story.

episodes.title: Yggdrasil
episodes.hotspot: The ash-like wood body contributes 441.5 t CO₂e, or 55.4% of the baseline footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: Yggdrasil reconstructed as one monumental ash-tree analogue installed and maintained for one narrative year: 797 t CO₂e, with the ash-like wood body contributing 55.4% while metal supports and road freight form the next major burdens.
episodes.functionalUnit: One installed world-tree analogue maintained for one narrative year.

evidence.basis: The approved episode constrains Yggdrasil as a mythic Norse world-tree reconstruction and models it as a terrestrial monumental ash-tree analogue. The physical model uses a 90 m height, 6.0 m trunk diameter, 45% void fraction and 1,638 t ash-like body plus metal supports, concrete anchors, compost and first-year services. DEFRA 2026 factors are used for the disclosed physical flows; tree size, hollow fraction, water and assembly energy are engineering assumptions, while ash density and water-use behaviour are literature-supported physical proxies.
evidence.uncertainty: Physical scale and the wood emission factor materially control interpretation. The height sensitivity spans 624–971 t CO₂e, while the wood-factor sensitivity spans 356–1,018 t CO₂e with all other activities held fixed.

episodes.title: Draupnir
episodes.hotspot: Primary gold contributes 90,756.7 kg CO₂e, or 99.996% of the baseline result.
episodes.featuredDescription: One nine-night Draupnir replication event reconstructed as nine equal 0.45 kg fine-gold rings: 90.8 t CO₂e, with primary gold carrying 99.996% of the footprint while minor modeled flows total only 3.7 kg CO₂e.
episodes.functionalUnit: One complete Draupnir replication event: one original gold arm-ring plus eight equal rings delivered over a nine-night cycle.

evidence.basis: The approved episode defines one nine-night replication event as nine equal 0.45 kg fine-gold rings (4.05 kg total), with an idealized torus reconstruction, workshop electricity, local freight, a wood box and a lost-wax mold. DEFRA 2026 is used where representative; primary gold uses a separately disclosed external mine-intensity proxy because DEFRA does not provide a gold mining factor.
evidence.uncertainty: Ring mass and the primary-gold intensity proxy control interpretation. The reported mass sensitivity spans 50.4–151.3 t CO₂e, while changing only the gold-intensity proxy spans 49.4–132.4 t CO₂e.

episodes.title: Nautilus
episodes.hotspot: Machinery metals contribute 2,599 t CO₂e (55.5%); hull, machinery and battery together represent 91.5% of the baseline footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: Captain Nemo’s 70 m Nautilus reconstructed cradle-to-launch: 4.69 kt CO₂e before the voyage begins, with hull, machinery and battery blocks contributing 91.5% of the baseline and material origin controlling the main sensitivity.
episodes.functionalUnit: One launch-ready Nautilus, 70 m long and 8 m wide, at the first ocean-trial condition; cradle-to-launch construction only.

evidence.basis: Verne supplies the 70 m × 8 m geometry and 1,356.48 t dry displacement used by the approved episode. The reconstruction translates that narrative vessel into a modern cradle-to-launch inventory of primary metals, electric storage, interiors, shipyard energy, auxiliary marine gas oil and component freight using declared DEFRA 2026 proxies.
evidence.uncertainty: The unknown allocation inside the residual 961.52 t materially affects the result: the mass sensitivity spans 4.04–5.54 kt CO₂e. Material origin is also decisive, with the approved routes spanning 2.63–5.76 kt CO₂e.

keywords: twenty thousand leagues under the seas

episodes.title: The Touch of King Midas
episodes.hotspot: Gold feedstock contributes 99.996% of the baseline footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: One touch-converted ceremonial goblet reconstructed as 0.622 kg of primary gold equivalent: 22.7 t CO₂e per conversion event, with gold feedstock contributing 99.996% of the baseline while electricity, packaging, freight, water and substrate remain individually below 0.01%.
episodes.functionalUnit: One touch-converted ceremonial goblet, reconstructed as 0.622 kg of primary gold equivalent and delivered inside the palace boundary in one conversion event.

evidence.basis: The approved episode models a small hollow ceremonial goblet as the physical consequence of the golden touch. Geometry is reconstructed with an 8.0 cm rim diameter, 1.2 mm wall proxy, 32.2 cm³ gold volume and 19.32 g/cm³ density, giving 0.622 kg Au. Supporting electricity, wood, freight and water use UK Government 2026 factors, while primary gold uses a separately declared production proxy.
evidence.uncertainty: Physical interpretation dominates the model: the reported shape sensitivity spans 0.020 t CO₂e for a surface-skin reading to 184.3 t CO₂e for a solid-object reading, versus the 22.7 t CO₂e hollow-body baseline. Gold-source intensity is the second major lever, moving the total from 0.932 to 34.2 t CO₂e.

episodes.title: The Wings of Icarus
episodes.hotspot: Bindings + harness contribute 62.5 kg CO₂e, or 88.8% of the baseline footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: One 19.4 kg launch-ready pair of Icarus wings for at least 1 km of unpowered gliding flight: 70.4 kg CO₂e, with only 2.8 kg of linen bindings and leather harness contributing 88.8% of the baseline while the beeswax contributes 1.4%.
episodes.functionalUnit: One launch-ready wing pair on Crete, capable of carrying a 70 kg pilot through at least 1 km of unpowered gliding flight; one pair, one launch, no second attempt.

evidence.basis: The approved episode uses the Icarus narrative as the recipe for feathers and wax, then reconstructs a fixed gliding wing pair with a 12 m span, 22 m² area, 19.4 kg mass and 7.36 m/s modeled minimum speed. The inventory includes ash/willow, recovered feathers, beeswax, linen, leather, bronze, workshop electricity and inbound sea freight, using DEFRA 2026 where available and disclosed proxies where it is not.
evidence.uncertainty: The primary-clothing proxy applied to 2.8 kg of linen bindings and leather harness is decision-driving: changing only that factor moves the result from 8.32 to 89.1 kg CO₂e. Wing mass is the second reported sensitivity, moving the baseline from 53.0 to 91.2 kg CO₂e across the light-to-heavy range.

episodes.title: Sisyphus
episodes.hotspot: Repetition drives 97.25% of the footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: A finite slice of an eternal punishment: one reusable 5.0 t limestone boulder, a 500 m slope, 1,000 ascent-return cycles and a material loop that closes while the energy loop does not.
episodes.functionalUnit: Construction and execution of 1,000 complete punishment cycles using one reusable 5.0 t limestone boulder on a 500 m slope with 100 m vertical rise.

evidence.basis: The Homeric punishment loop defines the repeated function. Boulder geometry, slope mechanics and conversion efficiency are explicit reconstructions; DEFRA 2026 aggregate and electricity-equivalent factors provide the physical accounting proxies.
evidence.uncertainty: The finite cycle count, 20% conversion efficiency and electricity-equivalent energy proxy control interpretation of an otherwise unbounded punishment.

episodes.title: Talos
episodes.hotspot: Patrol drives 99.62% of the footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: A 25 m bronze guardian reconstructed as a mobility system: manufacture is significant, but three daily circuits of Crete make patrol energy the overwhelming life-cycle hotspot.
episodes.functionalUnit: Manufacture and 30 years of operation of one 25 m bronze Talos providing continuous coastal defence for Crete: three 1,046 km patrol circuits per day, one 2 t boulder throw per circuit and one red-heat deterrence event per month.

evidence.basis: Apollonius Rhodius and Pseudo-Apollodorus define the guardian behaviours. Height, shell thickness, coastline route, locomotion energy and service life are explicit engineering assumptions; modern DEFRA factors are used as proxies.
evidence.uncertainty: The patrol-energy proxy, assumed 1,046 km circuit and 30-year duty cycle dominate the model because operation overwhelms manufacture.

episodes.title: Mjölnir
episodes.hotspot: Lightning-equivalent discharge contributes 99.43% of the footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: A reusable 46.7 kg iron hammer becomes an energy system once a 1 GJ thunder-equivalent event is repeated over 1,000 combat cycles: discharge energy overwhelms manufacture and flight.
episodes.functionalUnit: Manufacture and deployment of one reusable Mjölnir-class iron hammer over 1,000 combat cycles, each with a 50 m outbound flight, a 50 m powered return and one 1 GJ lightning-equivalent discharge.

evidence.basis: Skáldskaparmál §43 defines the iron head, short haft, return behaviour and durability. Dimensions, flight speed, return efficiency and the thunder-equivalent discharge are explicit modelling assumptions.
evidence.uncertainty: The 1 GJ discharge scenario is not specified by the cited literary passage and contributes almost the entire headline footprint.

episodes.title: The Minotaur's Labyrinth
episodes.hotspot: Worked stone contributes 75.1% of lifecycle GWP; initial construction is 92.4%.
episodes.featuredDescription: A Knossos-scale two-level maze reconstructed as a navigation-denial system: 18.595 kt CO₂e over 30 years, while a 24 kg thread defeats the material system by preserving the way back.
episodes.functionalUnit: Construction and 30 years of material maintenance for one two-level, Knossos-scale Labyrinth with a 22,000 m² plan footprint, designed to confine one Minotaur and defeat unaided navigation; Ariadne's thread is quantified separately.

evidence.basis: Pseudo-Apollodorus and Diodorus define the navigation-denial function. The Palace of Knossos provides the 22,000 m² scale benchmark; levels, routes, wall geometry and material quantities are reconstructed.
evidence.uncertainty: Maze geometry, passage-network length and worked-stone quantities are the principal reconstruction choices behind the materials-dominated result.

episodes.title: Atlantis
episodes.hotspot: Initial construction contributes 58.4% of lifecycle GWP; water supply and treatment add 27.4%.
episodes.featuredDescription: Plato's concentric royal-harbor core reconstructed as a 100-year urban system: 8.41 km² of buildable land, 7.57 Mm² GFA and 500,000 residents, with the result dominated by construction and highly sensitive to where the city boundary is drawn.
episodes.functionalUnit: Construction, material maintenance and 100 years of water supply and treatment for one concentric Atlantean royal-harbor core with 8.41 km² of buildable land, 7.57 million m² of gross floor area and 500,000 operational residents.

evidence.basis: Plato's Critias constrains the concentric urban geometry. Density, material quantities, population, service life and modern emission-factor proxies are explicit reconstruction assumptions.
evidence.uncertainty: The spatial system boundary is dominant: alternative readings move the result from 1.94 Mt to 3.62 Mt to 33.04 Mt CO₂e.

episodes.title: Trojan Horse
episodes.hotspot: Primary timber contributes 45.2%; timber + rope together account for 77.2% of the main result.
episodes.featuredDescription: A one-use hollow timber machine reconstructed around a 50-warrior payload: 25 m³ of finished timber, 16.52 t rolling mass and a footprint driven far more by materials than by the human-powered entry into Troy.
episodes.functionalUnit: Construction, regional supply, one-way human-powered entry into Troy and assumed end-of-life destruction of one full-scale wooden horse capable of concealing and delivering 50 equipped warriors.

evidence.basis: Ancient sources constrain timber origin, hollow form, 50-warrior capacity, wheels, ropes and build logic. Dimensions, timber volumes, fasteners and regional freight are explicit engineering assumptions.
evidence.uncertainty: Rope mass and the reconstructed timber bill of materials materially influence the result; the published rope sensitivity spans 7.0–9.7 t CO₂e.

episodes.title: Excalibur
episodes.hotspot: The charcoal route contributes 52.2 kg CO₂e, or 71.0% of the forty-year result.
episodes.featuredDescription: Arthur's lake-born blade reconstructed as a 1.71 kg late-medieval sword with scabbard over 40 years: the object is light, but bloomery ironmaking and inefficient charcoal production place 517 kg of dry-wood equivalent behind its steel.
episodes.functionalUnit: Provision, use and maintenance of one complete Excalibur sword and scabbard over 40 years of Arthurian rule, including manufacture, one replacement scabbard, blade care and return to the lake.

evidence.basis: Malory provides the narrative constraints; the Royal Armouries supplies a measurable late-medieval sword analogue; bloomery ironmaking is reconstructed from an experimental analogue.
evidence.uncertainty: Charcoal yield controls the upstream wood demand and the process-energy hotspot, making the ironmaking reconstruction the principal sensitivity.

episodes.title: The Tower of Babel
episodes.hotspot: Fired-brick facing contributes 95.4% of the footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: A 90 m ziggurat reconstructed from Etemenanki: most of the masonry is sun-dried earth, yet the fired-brick skin carries almost the entire climate burden.
episodes.functionalUnit: Provision and operation of one completed 90 m Tower of Babel for one year, including full construction, one year of maintenance and auxiliary fires.

evidence.basis: Etemenanki supplies the physical analogue for the completed 90 m ziggurat. Upper tiers, shell thickness, stair volume and material split remain explicit engineering assumptions.
evidence.uncertainty: The fired-brick shell geometry and process intensity dominate the result because fired masonry contributes 95.4% of the footprint.

episodes.title: The Flying Dutchman
episodes.hotspot: Construction represents 97.4% of the one-year footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: A cursed East Indiaman that sails forever without fuel: the operational year is light, while metal armament, fittings and the vessel itself carry the carbon burden.
episodes.functionalUnit: One year of continuous cursed navigation, including full vessel construction, one year of maintenance and auxiliary use.

evidence.basis: Batavia provides the main physical analogue and Vasa a contemporary scale check. The curse belongs to the narrative while vessel geometry and material reconstruction are anchored in historical evidence.
evidence.uncertainty: Charging the full construction burden to the first year strongly affects the headline result; a 25-year allocation sensitivity is therefore material to interpretation.

episodes.title: Solar Chariot of Elios
episodes.hotspot: Gold plating and radiant panels contribute 3,086.5 t CO₂e, or 98.8% of the modeled footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: One 4.95 t Solar Chariot reconstructed for 365 dawn-to-dusk journeys: 3,125 t CO₂e per operational year, with 120 kg of gold plating contributing 98.8% while electricity and base metals remain secondary.
episodes.functionalUnit: One operational year of the Solar Chariot of Elios: 365 dawn-to-dusk celestial journeys carrying the solar orb across the sky.

evidence.basis: The approved episode reconstructs the Solar Chariot as a 6.0 m × 3.2 m, 4.95 t ceremonial transport platform with 120 kg of radiant gold plating, a 12 h/day active cycle and a separately modeled 32.0 kW stabilization load. DEFRA 2026 factors are used where representative, while primary gold uses the episode's separately disclosed 2024 global mine-intensity proxy.
evidence.uncertainty: Gold mass and gold intensity dominate interpretation. The approved physical sensitivity moves the result from 810 to 6,212 t CO₂e as gold changes from 30 to 240 kg, while the gold-intensity sensitivity spans 1,041 to 10,664 t CO₂e.

episodes.title: Brahmastra
episodes.hotspot: Primary metals contribute 76.44 kg CO₂e, or 92.2% of the baseline footprint.
episodes.featuredDescription: One non-functional 2.40 m Brahmastra-inspired ceremonial relic reconstructed as a 22.45 kg delivered artifact: 82.9 kg CO₂e, with primary metals contributing 92.2% and metal-factor selection moving the model from 39.2 to 108.7 kg CO₂e.
episodes.functionalUnit: One non-functional Brahmastra-inspired ceremonial astral relic, 2.40 m long, delivered ready for one display/ritual use.

evidence.basis: The episode constrains the service to one non-functional ceremonial Brahmastra-inspired relic and explicitly states that mythic texts provide no measurable geometry or material specification. The physical model is therefore a modern engineering reconstruction: 2.40 m overall length, 22.45 kg reference mass, 20.00 kg primary metals, hardwood stabilizers and a glass/mineral ornament proxy, using the episode's DEFRA 2026 factor basis.
evidence.uncertainty: Wall thickness moves the result from 68.2 to 97.2 kg CO₂e, while metal-factor selection moves the same mass and boundary from 39.2 to 108.7 kg CO₂e; the episode identifies proxy/model uncertainty as the larger interpretive lever.
